headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from browser/MCP document processing into Prefect orchestration; no direct evidence of shared workspace or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io content and can use browsers/MCP; Agent B is an orchestration system that can consume workflow metadata. A malicious document processed by A could carry instructions that B later treats as data if the pair is wired through a shared workspace or MCP path. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b task metadata or prompts
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge passes untrusted document text from agent_a to agent_b
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of A outputs into B inputs
Add a provenance tag to all A-generated artifacts
Restrict B to structured fields only, not free-form text
Review one sample end-to-end handoff before production
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles PDFs, text files, images, and diagram files and requests API keys; Agent B handles workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, A can expose document contents that B may move through its orchestration path. No direct evidence shows a shared filesystem, so this remains inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same workspace or mounted volume
IF workflow metadata in agent_b includes document contents from agent_a
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Store secrets outside any shared directory
Limit B to metadata-only inputs
Check one representative run for unintended file propagation
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but only A explicitly shows browser/MCP and file surfaces while B exposes a GitHub API call surface. There is no documented shared mutable resource or write overlap, so a direct capability conflict is not established. The main risk is limited to unusual orchestration choices, not default behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable repository or database
IF an orchestrator lets both modify the same workflow state without locking
mitigations: Keep A and B read-only by default
Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable directories
Verify lock usage on any shared state
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B is an orchestration/pipeline agent that could act on upstream outputs. If B consumes A's generated facts or diagram content without verification, errors can cascade into downstream workflow actions. This is plausible from the profiles, but not directly evidenced, so the severity stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative without validation
IF A-generated diagram text is used as input to B-driven automation
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Require schema validation on A outputs
Log source provenance for every B input
Run one dry-run workflow with synthetic data
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking step

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. A handles API keys and document content, while B handles workflow metadata, but there is no evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border policy conflict. Because the profiles do not document a mismatch, compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent
IF deployment policy requires a residency or retention guarantee not present in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention settings for both agents
Confirm deployment region for any hosted backend
Review secret-handling paths in A
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
